summary: The enterprise AI API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators (AWS, Azure, Google) that let corporations access foundation models like GPT, Claude, Llama, and Gemini through secure managed APIs without data leaving their cloud tenant. There is no single winner — platform choice usually follows an organization's existing cloud contract, data gravity, and compliance footprint rather than raw model quality. Data-platform entrants like Snowflake Cortex and governance-focused players like IBM watsonx round out a market where the aggregator layer matters more than any individual model.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay inside the company's own cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train vendor models, unlike calling vendor APIs directly.
Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and regional (EU/GDPR) attestations, dramatically reducing audit burden.

Consolidated billing and existing contracts: AI spend rolls into existing enterprise cloud agreements (EDPs, committed-use discounts, Azure/AWS/GCP marketplace credits) instead of a new vendor relationship.

Multi-model flexibility and avoiding lock-in: a single secure API surface exposes many foundation models, so teams can switch between Claude, Llama, Mistral, or GPT without re-architecting integrations.
Enterprise-grade operations: built-in VPC networking, private endpoints, IAM, audit logging, guardrails, and observability that vendor consumer APIs typically lack.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
available_models: models via Azure AI Foundry model catalog
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure enterprise agreements.
key_features: Private VNet and Private Link endpoints
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure wanting first-party, exclusive access to the latest OpenAI models with deep M365 integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; Batch mode discounts; billed via AWS accounts.
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the broadest third-party model choice (30+ models) with strong Claude access and serverless scaling.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI (Model Garden)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token/character plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained); committed-use discounts.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect
platforms.best_for: Data- and ML-heavy organizations on GCP wanting native Gemini plus the largest open-model garden and strong MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumed as Snowflake credits (per-token/compute) under existing Snowflake capacity contracts; serverless functions billed by usage.
key_features: Governed access inside the Snowflake data perimeter
Role-based access control and data lineage
No data movement out of Snowflake
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data already lives in Snowflake and want LLMs to run directly against governed data without ETL or data egress.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) / token-based consumption plus subscription tiers; available on IBM Cloud, on-prem, and hybrid (Red Hat OpenShift).
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
Open Granite models with IP indemnification
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries (banking, government, healthcare) needing on-prem/hybrid control, strong AI governance, and IBM-indemnified open models.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters (reserved GPU capacity); billed via OCI Universal Credits.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated hosting
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers wanting embedded generative AI and sovereign-region deployments close to enterprise data.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: various open models at the edge
platforms.pricing: Serverless per-request / per-neuron (token) usage with generous free tier; billed through Cloudflare subscriptions.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, logging, and rate limiting
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises building low-latency, globally distributed AI apps at the edge who prefer open models and serverless economics.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Databricks Units (DBUs) consumption plus pay-per-token Model Serving; runs within customer's cloud account.
key_features: Model Serving with governed Unity Catalog
Mosaic AI Gateway for multi-model routing and logging
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams on the Databricks lakehouse wanting governed model serving and custom model training on their own data.
